Its weak, frame-free form is a bare cardinality or indeterminate-amount word anywhere in a sentence - cardinal numerals ('two', 'three', 'four', 'six', 'eight', 'twenty', 'dozen') and amount words ('plenty', 'a lot', 'dozens', 'tons', 'amount', 'quantity', 'few', 'several', 'little') at about 20-45% of max - plus the comparative particle 'than' after a comparative ('more than', 'less than', 'more X than') at 40-65%. It stays at baseline on definite or anaphoric subjects with the same copulas ('they are', 'the bridge is', 'it is', 'that is'), on non-existential 'there' ('over there'; 'three bridges are there'), on inverted questions ('Is there ...?'), and on universal/partitive quantifiers and degree adverbs ('all', 'each', 'every', 'both', 'some', 'more', 'most', 'very', 'quite', 'first', 'second').
